notes: How this part was researched: the session's shared web-search allowance ran out after the first fifteen candidates (through Jim Godfrey). The rest were researched by opening pages directly: each city's, county's and school district's own site, the Minnesota DFL's list and local party units' own pages, the Legislative Reference Library, the University of Minnesota's election archive, and local newspapers' own election sections. A campaign site reached by trying an address was kept only when its own pages name the candidate and the office; addresses that turned out not to be campaign sites for these races were dropped.

The Minnesota Judicial Branch's site (mncourts.gov) refuses scripts (403 to robots.txt and to pages), so no court page was read. Nothing is recorded for Kevin M. Miller; Paul Thissen's facts come from the Legislature's library, whose record of him also gives his appointment.
Stearns County's own commissioner pages are drawn by script and showed no text, so Bob Johnson has no official page here and his offices rest on MPR News and St. Cloud LIVE.

No Republican endorsement could be recorded: mngop.com lists statewide nominees only, the Senate District 41 Republicans' site announces its endorsing convention (March 28, 2026) without the result, and the Scott County Republicans' endorsed-candidates page refused the script (403). The DFL's list names no Senate candidate for District 38 (Susan Pha), and names Dan Mitchell for 5A with a link to a social media page only, which is not a campaign website.

The Minnesota Historical Election Archive (University of Minnesota Libraries) is the source for three earlier runs under a party label (Jim Godfrey in 2008 and 2010; the 2025 special primary in House District 34B). It is a university archive of official returns, not a news organization, and is labelled secondary for the second reader to judge. The birth dates it shows were not taken, because the source it names for them is a birth records index.

Two candidates share a name with a better-known person (Sarah Anderson in Plymouth; Ellie Krug in Eastern Carver County). No page ties either candidate to that other record, and Sarah Anderson's own campaign site does not claim it, so nothing was taken from those records.

Matthew Thompson: the ROCORI district writes its sitting board member's name Matt Thompson (term through December 31, 2026). Sara Herr Larsen: the Milaca board page writes Sara Larsen and the district's campaign finance report list writes Sara Herr-Larsen.

Nothing citable was found for John G Pioske, Kim Frederick, George Hanson, Celeste Koppe, Ellie Krug, Kim L. Hudson, Bopha Sar and Kevin M. Miller. The news profiles read for them (Henderson Independent, Detroit Lakes Tribune, KAXE, Red Wing Republican Eagle) name no public office held and no campaign website; what they say of work and household is not recorded.

Verifier, 2026-10-02: every address in this file was re-opened with the kit's own User-Agent and the quoted words looked for on the page. 60 findings checked, 58 kept, 2 removed (see removed), 5 reworded (see corrected). The DFL list is the party's own page, titled 'Candidates Endorsed by the Minnesota DFL'. Paul Thissen's and Aisha Gomez's sites name the candidate and the office but no 2026 date; Thissen's news items are from 2020. The Minnesota Historical Election Archive is neither official nor a news organization; it is kept under secondary, named as a university archive. Matt Thompson (ROCORI) and Sara Larsen (Milaca) are read as the candidates Matthew Thompson and Sara Herr Larsen: same board, a term ending with this election, and for Larsen the district's own Herr-Larsen spelling on the same page.
